Subject: Re: Redshifts shifted after upgrade to lumenfit 2.5.0?

@kpd_wrangler, I did read the changelog. I’ve now traced the offset to PR #812, and I’d like to ask that this thread be reopened.

In 2.5.0, PR #812 changed the default in LineList.__init__ from wave_frame='air' to wave_frame='vacuum'. My spectra are calibrated in air, so the new default uses vacuum rest wavelengths against air wavelengths in the data. Around H-alpha, the vacuum-to-air wavelength ratio is approximately 1.00028, consistent with the redshift offset I reported, or about 83 km/s.

For anyone else encountering this, the workaround that fixes my case is to set the frame explicitly:

LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Please use the frame appropriate to your own data.

I’m frustrated that this was dismissed as a calibration or configuration problem and marked solved without investigating the version change. I spent two days thinking my wavelength calibration was broken and re-reduced arc lamps for 40 spectra unnecessarily. m_okonkwo also reported seeing an offset in the same thread, so mine may not be an isolated case.

“Works for me” doesn’t test whether this default change affects air-calibrated optical spectra. If your data and line list already use vacuum wavelengths, for example, you might not see the same difference.

The 2.5.0 changelog describes #812 as a “refactor” of LineList and spectral frame handling; it does not say that the default changed, and there was no deprecation warning. Could a maintainer please reopen this thread and add an explicit line to CHANGES.md about the changed default, or add a warning when wave_frame is not set? That would help others identify the issue without repeating these checks.
